Subject: Spike on April 12th invoice - hold & logs request

Hi Markus,

We put your last invoice on hold after seeing a ~7x jump in billed token units on April 12th (invoice #ACME-0427). This doesn’t match our production telemetry — we have a stable request volume for that day. Can you please: 

- Confirm whether there was a known platform event or migration on 4/12 that could explain the sampling increase.
- Share the raw ingest/session traces (or a short sample) and any request IDs for the biggest sessions.
- Tell us how Redwood attributes streaming vs non-streaming tokens (we suspect double-counting of partial streams).

I attached a brief CSV export from our side (acme-usage-snapshot-20270412.csv). We’ve paused payment until we understand the variance. If this is a billing error we’ll need a credit and a note for our AP team.

Thanks,
Clara Reynolds
Head of Billing Operations
Acme Solutions

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike on April 12th invoice - hold & logs request

Hi Clara — thanks for flagging this and for the CSV. 

Short answer: we don’t have any scheduled migrations or global incidents on 4/12 that would explain a wholesale multiplier. I’ve started a scoped audit on the usage ledger for ACME and attached a tiny sample export of our ingest records that map to the window you highlighted.

Next steps I’m putting in motion:
- Priyom (cc) will pull session-trace bundles and look for repeated replays/duplicate request ids.
- Ben will run a token attribution pass to check for streaming boundary double-counts.
- I’ll share a proposed preliminary credit if we find a clear attribution error.

A couple of housekeeping q’s that will speed things up:
1) Can you share the earliest request_id you see in your CSV for the spike? If you can paste one or two rows that would make correlation much faster.
2) Do you have any bots/ingest backfills on April 12th we should know about?

I attached: redwood-ingest-sample-20270412.json (small sample, 2MB) — this maps timestamps -> request_id -> token counts.

We’ll aim to get a preliminary finding within 48 hours. Apologies for the friction — we want to resolve this quickly so your AP team can proceed.

— Markus Klein
Senior Manager, Customer Billing
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-ingest-sample-20270412.json (JSON, 2MB)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: finance-ops@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike on April 12th invoice - proposed remediation for ACME

Team — forwarding ACME thread with a short remediation proposal so we can coordinate approval and issuance of a credit memo. Summary of our findings (prelim):

- Root cause: sampling replay on a long-running streaming session. One client SDK version (v1.3.4) can prematurely retry stream fragments when a short-lived TCP drop occurs; our token aggregator counted fragments as separate sessions in the ledger. Roughly 2.6M tokens double-counted across ~180 sessions.
- Impact: ~$1,200 of billable tokens on the April 12th invoice (post-tier pricing).
- Short-term remediation for the customer: issue a pro-rated credit of $1,200 and mark invoice ACME-0427 as "adjusted" so they can release the payment hold.
- Long-term: backfill token-attribution change in the ledger to deduplicate streaming fragments and ship a minor runtime patch to the SDK.

Attachments: credit-proposal-ACME-20270414.xlsx (proposed credit memo + breakdown), session-traces-20270412.tar.gz (internal trace bundle)

Questions for Finance Ops:
- Please confirm GL code to use for the credit memo and whether a negative invoice or a standalone credit is preferable for our accounting flow.
- Can we auto-issue the credit pending a short QA window, or do we need exec sign-off for credits > $1,000?

If you want the full trace bundle unredacted send me a secure link request — I can share on a restricted S3 URL.

Thanks,
Markus
